# API Requirements Quality Checklist: Lichess Puzzle

**Purpose**: Validate that the Puzzle requirements (loading, validation, navigation, SAN) are complete, clear and consistent enough to implement test-first
**Created**: 2026-10-03
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Does the spec define how a mapping input with missing keys or extra keys is handled? [Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 - Does the spec state whether mapping values must be strings or may already be typed (e.g. `int` rating)? [Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is the behavior for a malformed DailyDate (non-ISO, impossible date) specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-005, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are validation rules specified for PuzzleId and GameUrl (e.g. empty values)? [Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK005 - Is the type of error raised on invalid data specified, or deliberately left to the plan? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK006 - Does the spec define whether the exposed position is independent of the puzzle's internal state, so caller changes can't corrupt navigation? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 - Is the minimum move count stated precisely (only "empty" is named; is a single move also invalid)? [Ambiguity, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is "the bad field" defined for whole-row failures such as the wrong field count, where no single field is at fault? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the criterion for recognising "the CSV header itself" defined, or is it expected to fail through ordinary field validation? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the representation of a "move" in the public API specified (UCI string vs move object) for `moves`, next move and previous move? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is the Popularity range -100..100 a validation rule or informational only? [Ambiguity, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is the treatment of leading/trailing whitespace inside numeric and date fields specified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is "tell the caller no move was made" specified as a return value, exception or other signal? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK014 - Is FR-004's "ordered lists" consistent with the data model's immutable tuples, and is either acceptable to the spec? [Conflict, Spec §FR-004, data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is "solver's first turn (step 1)" in FR-010 consistent with US2 scenario 2's description of step 1? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, US2]
- [ ] CHK016 - Do the edge-case error rules (FR-013) and SC-005 cover the same set of invalid cases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK017 - Is the "Status: Draft" spec consistent with a plan that treats every clarification as resolved? [Consistency]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK018 - Is "for any valid puzzle" in SC-002 bounded to a defined set of test puzzles so it can be verified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK019 - Does SC-001 list the expected value for every one of the 11 fields, including the FEN and the derived solver side? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, US1]
- [ ] CHK020 - Does US1 scenario 4 give a concrete example row with opening tags and a daily date and their expected values? [Measurability, Spec US1]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 - Are SAN expectations defined for special moves (castling, promotion, en passant, checkmate suffix)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK022 - Are requirements defined for UCI promotion moves (e.g. `e7e8q`) and UCI castling notation in the Moves field? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK023 - Is it specified whether a puzzle must end on a solver move (move-count parity), or is any length ≥ 2 valid? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK024 - Are repeated or out-of-order navigation calls (e.g. jumping to the current step) addressed? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK025 - Is the assumption that every row has 11 columns including DailyDate checked against the current Lichess export format? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK026 - Is the assumption that every FEN is a standard-chess (non-Chess960) position stated? [Assumption, Gap]
- [ ] CHK027 - Is it stated that SAN formatting rules (check `+`, mate `#`, disambiguation) are whatever python-chess produces? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK028 - Are equality, hashing and string representation of a puzzle deliberately out of scope or missing? [Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
